The Federal Government’s Decade of Gas programme has taken its capacity-building drive to NLNG Limited’s facility on Bonny Island, Rivers State, exposing 35 young professionals to gas processing, liquefaction, storage and export operations. The participants, drawn from different parts of Nigeria’s oil and gas industry, recently toured NLNG’s operational Trains 1 to 6 and the ongoing Train 7 expansion project as part of efforts to develop local expertise for the country’s planned gas-powered economy. According to a statement on Wednesday, the visit, held in Port Harcourt and Bonny, was led by the Coordinating Director of the Decade of Gas Secretariat, Mr Ed Ubong, and hosted by NLNG’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Engr Adeleye Falade, alongside members of the company’s leadership team. Speaking during the visit, Ubong said the programme was designed to complement classroom training with practical exposure to industrial operations. “What we are building is not just knowledge, but confidence and competence. You cannot drive a gas-powered economy from theory alone. Our young professionals must see, touch and understand how gas is processed, liquefied, stored and exported to the world,” Ubong said. He described NLNG as an important part of Nigeria’s gas development strides and said the visit would help participants understand the standards required to operate large-scale gas facilities. “NLNG is the pride of Nigeria’s gas story. Bringing these 35 young talents here is intentional. We want them to see what excellence looks like, to ask questions, and to return to their organisations with a new mindset about what is possible for Nigeria,” he added. According to Ubong, the programme is developing engineers, geoscientists, commercial analysts and policymakers who will drive gas-based industrialisation, power generation, liquefied petroleum gas penetration, compressed natural gas adoption and gas-to-chemicals projects. These are the people who will deliver the Decade of Gas vision, not just as employees, but as leaders, innovators and problem-solvers for the country,” Ubong stressed. In his remarks, Falade said the company was pleased to host the young professionals, noting that human capital development remained critical to building a sustainable gas economy. That is why we are delighted to host this group of bright young professionals,” Falade noted. He said NLNG’s operations, from Trains 1 to 6 to the ongoing Train 7 expansion project, demonstrate the technical capacity Nigerians could develop through sustained investment, innovation and partnerships. Falade urged the participants to see themselves as contributors to the next phase of the country’s gas development, while maintaining high standards of safety, sustainability and local content in their careers. “What you have seen on Bonny Island is what Nigerians can build and sustain when we are committed to excellence and safety. As you go back, I want you to carry this spirit, that Nigeria can lead in gas, not just in Africa, but globally,” Falade stated. He also urged the professionals to recognise the importance of their future decisions to the country’s ability to harness its estimated gas reserves of more than 200 trillion cubic feet. “The future of Nigeria’s gas industry is in your hands. The decisions you will make in the next 10 years will determine whether we fully harness our 200+ trillion cubic feet of gas reserves for power, industry, jobs and prosperity,” he said. According to the statement, the visit featured technical sessions on LNG production processes, plant integrity, health, safety and environment, shipping and export logistics, as well as interactive engagements with NLNG engineers and managers. Participants reportedly described the experience as an important learning opportunity, saying it had improved their understanding of the gas value chain. They said the tour had broadened their perspectives, describing it as more than just a programme but a career-defining experience. “The Decade of Gas Programme, is deliberately positioning natural gas as the cornerstone of Nigeria’s energy transition, economic diversification and industrial growth. This is in line with President Bola Tinubu commitment that Gas must provide prosperity for all Nigerians. “With capacity building as a key pillar, the secretariat says the Bonny visit is one of several immersive learning experiences planned for the cohort, which will also include engagements with regulators, upstream producers, and gas infrastructure companies,” the statement concluded.
